meta.title: The APAC SC motion
meta.source: Internal rollout deck for the SC team. Rebuild with sc-deck: python skills/sc-deck/scripts/build_deck.py rollout/overview/deck.json --render

slides.title: One good way to prepare every customer meeting
slides.subtitle: The APAC SC motion, run with Claude
slides.notes: Five minutes. The point: same quality from every SC, less time on preparation, and every deal makes the next one easier.

reasons.title: Same quality from every SC
reasons.text: Every first meeting, demo and requirements pack starts from the same standard, whoever runs it.

reasons.title: Hours, not days
reasons.text: Claude does the preparation: research, deck, fit-gap, demo plan. You spend your time on the customer.

reasons.title: Every demo makes the next easier
reasons.text: Each build goes into a shared library within 2 working days, so nobody starts from zero.

reasons.title: It gets better every week
reasons.text: Meeting reviews and your feedback feed a Friday digest. Renzo approves at most 3 changes a week.

slides.title: The motion, from first call to proof
slides.subtitle: The flow

steps.title: First meeting
steps.what: Call transcript in. Prep, the standard deck and a light config out (sc-first-meeting)

steps.title: Requirements
steps.what: RFP or TOR in Indonesia: a fit-gap (sc-rfp). Australia: 2-hour workshops (sc-workshop)

steps.title: Demo plan
steps.what: Three questions, the demo bar, Business Studio first, then AI (sc-demo-plan)

steps.title: Build and click path
steps.what: The demo toolkit builds it. Then a practice page and a customer recap (sc-clickpath)

steps.title: Review and harvest
steps.what: What landed, what to change, and the build into the library (sc-meeting-review, sc-harvest)

slides.title: Before the first meeting
slides.subtitle: Step 1
slides.lead: From the BDR call to a meeting-ready deck in about an hour, not a day.

points.title: Prep
points.text: Company research with sources, likely pains for their industry, the questions to ask

points.title: The standard deck
points.text: Built from one deck.json per deal: what we heard, the platform, our starting idea, next steps

points.title: A light configuration
points.text: Half a day at most, so the first meeting shows their world, not a generic demo

slides.title: Requirements come from an RFP or a workshop
slides.subtitle: Step 2
slides.lead: Both end in one requirements register, rated honestly, that the demo plan builds from.

points.title: RFP or TOR (Indonesia)
points.text: Any layout in. Out come a fit-gap, a bid / no-bid view and a check of the bid team's answers before they submit

points.title: Workshops (Australia)
points.text: 2 hours, one journey each, starting from a draft they correct. A playback they sign off

points.title: Straight into the build
points.text: A POC brief and a solution model in Creatio terms, ready for the demo plan

slides.title: Plan the demo, build it, leave a trail
slides.subtitle: Steps 3 and 4
slides.lead: Every demo meets the same floor, the demo bar, and leaves room for your own ideas.

points.title: Three questions first
points.text: Who's the competition, what else has the customer given us, what else should we know

points.title: Business Studio first, then AI
points.text: Their words and data, opening on their outcome. Every AI moment has a person who confirms

points.title: A trail you can reuse
points.text: A click path to practise with and a customer recap that you approve before it's sent

slides.title: After every meeting, the motion learns
slides.subtitle: Step 5
slides.lead: Ten minutes after a meeting saves hours on the next one, yours and everyone else's.

points.title: Meeting review
points.text: What landed, what they corrected, the deck you actually presented, the next session's ideas

points.title: Harvest
points.text: The build goes into the demo library within 2 working days, the AI included

points.title: Your feedback
points.text: Say "feedback: …" whenever something doesn't work. It reaches Friday's digest

reasons.title: Your check, always
reasons.text: Nothing reaches a customer until you've checked it. Recaps stay DRAFT until you approve them.

reasons.title: Claims from the catalogue
reasons.text: Proof points come only from the differentiator catalogue. AI, data and security answers only from the governance pack.

reasons.title: Tag the evidence
reasons.text: C they said it · I we inferred it · A we assumed it. Only C builds a scene straight away.

reasons.title: Ask before you build
reasons.text: The three questions before any configuration. A clean stand, rehearsed on the device you'll present with.

reasons.title: Never
reasons.text: Type passwords, register clio environments, open credentials files, or put build files in a deal folder.
